name: TPMS
description: Factory direct TPMS: a battery-powered pressure sensor on each valve stem transmits to the body control module/receiver. With the factory body electronics removed it serves no purpose; race cars either delete it or fit a motorsport TPMS that reports to the dash/logger.

components.name: TPMS sensors
components.description: Clamp-in sensor/valve assembly inside each wheel. Factory sensors must be relearned to the car (scan tool or pressure-change learn) after rotation.
components.location: Inside each wheel at the valve hole.

factory.name: GM TPMS sensor (direct, clamp-in)
factory.notes: Frequency/part number not confirmed in available sources (NA GM is typically 315 MHz – verify on your donor).

raceOptions.name: Delete (fit plain metal clamp-in valve stems)
raceOptions.notes: Saves ~30–40 g per wheel; disable TPMS warning in the dash/ECU strategy.

raceOptions.name: Motorsport TPMS (e.g. Bosch Motorsport, AiM, McLaren Applied/LDS)
raceOptions.notes: Reports pressure and temperature live to the dash/logger.

hardware.torque: ≈ 7 N·m (62 in-lb) typical GM clamp-in – verify

installNotes: Mount tire bead away from the sensor to avoid breaking it.

modelRef.dimensions: ~45 x 28 x 18 mm, sits on the drop well inside the tyre at the valve stem
modelRef.features: 315/433 MHz GM sensor body clamped to the valve stem

components.name: TPMS receiver / BCM function
components.description: Factory receiver function lives in the body control module/RF receiver; a motorsport TPMS uses its own receiver feeding CAN to the dash.
components.location: Factory: in body electronics. Race: receiver antenna centrally in cabin.
installNotes: Program sensor IDs into the receiver/dash.

modelRef.dimensions: Function inside the BCM / RF receiver – box is indicative only
